newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cattle passport, beef label plans face delay.
newsitem.headline: Cattle passport, beef label plans face delay.

text.p: Proposals to introduce cattle passports and beef labelling aimed at restoring consumer confidence damaged by the mad cow disease scare face long delay after the European Parliament demanded changes.

EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler opposed many of the proposed amendments and as the proposals are now being examined under the co-decision procedure -- Article 100A of the EU Treaty -- the Commission and parliament will have to find a compromise.
"The proposals are likely to be delayed many months," a parliament official said.
The parliament had been insisting on the need for speedy decisions to encourage consumers to return to beef.
On cattle identification (COM(96)0460), a report by Xavier Mayer (German, Christian Democrat), sought changes that would simplify the bureaucratic burden on farmers.

For instance it suggested doing away with cattle passports if the relevant information was stored on a computer data base by December 31, 1997. It also proposed that only data on birth and slaughtering should initially be registered.
On beef labelling (COM(96)0460), a report by Mihail Papayannakis (Greek, United Left) called for a compulsory system, which would be extended to beef products after one year.

But Fischler said that a voluntary system would be quicker to set up and should be followed during a transitional period until member states had set up computerised data bases and were ready to implement a compulsory system.
The Commission is also concerned that compulsory beef labelling could infringe international free trade rules.
